verdicts.title: Issue #373 closed without any fix: coarse GDP grids still silently erase detectable leakage
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. _MIN_GRID_SIZE = 16 at packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_estimate.py:37 and the only guard is `if grid_size < _MIN_GRID_SIZE: raise ValueError` at :176-177; `git show 79c916e3:.../_estimate.py` has the identical constant and guard, and `git log -S _MIN_GRID_SIZE -- packages/opaque-auditing` shows only the original 6cbe5520, so closed issue #373 landed no code change. Docs add nothing: docs/user-guide/auditing.md:103-110 and docs/reference/auditing.md:362-367,429-435 present grid_size as a tunable with no lower-bound guidance. Measured with the real GdpMethod (stub estimate, n_in=n_out=500): u=350 -> mu/eps = 0.0/0.0 (grid 16), 0.0/0.0 (64), 0.506/2.017 (256), 0.568/2.298 (10000); u=250 -> 0.0/0.0 (16), 0.655/2.700 (64), 1.142/5.108 (10000). So grid 16 does silently return eps=0 where the default returns 2.3-5.1, and the default costs 14-19 s per query, which is a real incentive to lower it. Severity cut from medium to low: the direction of the error is loose, not unsound -- a coarse grid over-estimates v_k, raises the Chernoff p-value, and yields a smaller mu-hat, so the returned value is still a *valid* (merely trivial) lower bound on epsilon and never inflates a privacy claim; it also requires the user to deliberately set grid_size three orders of magnitude below the default. affects_epsilon stays false for the same reason (no accountant/mechanism epsilon changes). Not a duplicate of any OPEN issue: #373 is closed, and open #376/#327 concern null calibration and the audit's statistical framing, not grid resolution.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user lowers grid_size to cut the ~15-19 s per-query cost of the default 10 000-point grid (docs advertise it as tunable with no floor guidance beyond the ValueError at <16). Verified in this session against the shipped GdpMethod: with 1000 canaries and 250 errors, gdp(grid_size=16).epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) returns 0.0 while grid_size=10000 returns 5.11; with 350 errors, grids 16 and 64 both return 0.0 versus 2.30 at the default. The audit reports no detectable leakage for a mechanism it would otherwise flag. The returned number remains a mathematically valid (if vacuous) lower bound, so nothing overstates privacy -- the loss is audit power, silently, under a configuration the API accepts.

verdicts.title: _mu_at hang fix is symptom-level: strong attacks with >2000 canary guesses now raise RuntimeError on the default epsilon_at surface
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on the default surface with the real code. _gdp.py:40 _MAX_EXACT_RANKS = 2000; :331-334 r_prime = min(r, 2000) and n_trunc = r - r_prime with truncated ranks fixed at v_k = 0.5; :384 expected = sum(v_k) + n_trunc*0.5. The structural consequence is exact: for r = 10000 the floor on the expectation is 4000 regardless of mu, so any u meaningfully below 4000 leaves the Chernoff bound under significance for every finite mu, and the :80-91 bracket loop exhausts _MAX_MU_BRACKET_DOUBLINGS and raises. Measured: GdpMethod(grid_size=10000) on a stub with n_in=n_out=5000 -- u=3800 raises RuntimeError('...for every mu up to 1.0289e+19...') after 100 s, while u=3900 returns mu=2.2485 / eps=11.56 in 25 s. OneRunEstimate.epsilon_at dispatches to gdp() (_estimate.py:197-201), so this is the default path, and the termination half of the fix is real (it raises rather than hangs). The limitation is undocumented: grep for '2000|truncat|_MAX_EXACT' over docs/user-guide/auditing.md and docs/reference/auditing.md returns nothing, while docs/user-guide/auditing.md:215-228 explicitly tabulates 10 000 / 100 000 / 1 000 000 canaries and says the ceiling table 'does not apply to the mu-GDP estimator', and recommends 5000+ canaries. Severity kept at medium: fail-closed with an actionable message and no wrong number emitted, but it blocks the documented recommended-scale workflow precisely in the high-leakage regime (>~61 % attack accuracy at m=10 000). affects_epsilon false -- no epsilon is produced at all. Adjacent to open #327 (rebuild empirical auditing around calibrated guarantees) but that issue is about statistical calibration, not the rank-truncation power cap, so not a duplicate.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A practitioner audits at the guide's recommended scale (m = 10 000 canaries) and the mechanism is badly under-noised, so the attack reaches ~62 % accuracy (u = 3800). Verified this session: estimate.epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) -- the default dispatch through gdp() -- raises RuntimeError after ~100 s of bracket doubling ('cannot invert mu-GDP p-value for (m=10000, r=10000, u=3800) ... use fewer canaries or a larger significance'), while a weaker attack at u = 3900 returns mu = 2.25 / eps = 11.56 normally. The cause is structural, not a search-bound artifact: with r - 2000 = 8000 truncated ranks pinned at v_k = 0.5 the expected error count can never fall below 4000, so no finite mu lifts the p-value to significance. The behaviour is fail-closed (no incorrect epsilon), but the 2000-rank truncation and the attack strength at which the estimator stops working are documented nowhere.

verdicts.title: OPQ-130 residual: 'Bonferroni (default)' comment still asserts a multiplicity correction that does not exist
verdicts.reasoning: Verified verbatim. packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_integration.py:42 reads '# Test epsilon with Bonferroni (default)' and :44 'assert eps_bonf > 0, "Bonferroni should also detect leakage"'. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for 'bonferroni' over packages/ and docs/ returns only these two lines plus an unrelated Poisson-sampler comment (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/sampling/test_poisson.py:18) and an unrelated accounting doc line. The path the test actually exercises is EpsDeltaMethod._epsilon_at (_eps_delta.py:60-79) at raw significance over (r, u) from OneRunEstimate._best_r_u, whose threshold-free branch is an unadjusted argmax over all empirical thresholds using the true labels (_estimate.py:159-161): 'correct = (self.n_in - self.fn_counts) + self.tn_counts; best_c = int(np.max(correct))'. No multiplicity correction exists anywhere. Severity is low and purely test/comment quality -- no computed value changes and no production code is affected. Kept already_tracked = 0: the underlying statistical defect (post-hoc threshold selection) is open #376, but this finding is the misleading naming in a test file, a distinct two-line cleanup that #376's title does not cover.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A maintainer investigating open issue #376 (post-hoc threshold selection in one-run auditing) greps for an existing multiplicity correction, finds the two 'Bonferroni' strings in test_integration.py, and momentarily concludes that multiple-threshold selection is already corrected for -- when the default path is an unadjusted argmax over all thresholds evaluated at raw significance. Pure documentation/test-comment drift: no computed epsilon, delta, or test outcome changes.

verdicts.title: fold_in's documented int/str domain disjointness is not structural: a 16-byte string collides with an integer fold
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. _engine.py:27-35 _stable_hash64 encodes an int as to_bytes(16, 'little', signed=True) + b'|' and any other value as str(part).encode('utf-8') + b'|', with no type discriminator, so the two paths share one byte stream. Executed: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed == fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15).seed -> both 2142789487919306769, True. That directly contradicts the docstring at :64-67 ('Integers and strings are hashed down disjoint paths ... no sequence of integer folds can reach a key derived through a string fold'), which the whole documented RNG convention rests on. Severity held at low and I would not raise it: reachability is essentially nil in practice. Colliding with a small caller integer (step, rank, leaf index) requires a string whose UTF-8 encoding is 15 NUL bytes plus one payload byte; colliding with a printable 16-byte ASCII tag requires the caller to fold an integer around 10^38, which nothing in Opaque does. Every internal stream root is a dotted-ASCII tag of non-16-byte length, so no current stream collides, and no epsilon is affected. The real defect is that a documented invariant users are told to rely on is enforced by convention rather than by encoding. Nothing in the open-issue snapshot covers it (#374 is closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: The docstring invariant at _engine.py:64-67 is false as written: because _stable_hash64 tags neither ints nor strs, fold_in(key(42), 1) and fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15) produce byte-identical keys (verified). The practical exposure is negligible -- a colliding string must encode to exactly 16 bytes matching the little-endian signed image of a folded integer, which for the small integers Opaque folds means a string of NUL bytes, and for a printable ASCII tag would require folding an integer near 10^38. No Opaque stream root collides today and no epsilon changes. The residual risk is that a third-party mechanism relying on the stated guarantee has no structural protection behind it; the fix is a one-byte type discriminator in _stable_hash64, or weakening the docstring claim.

verdicts.title: GPU lanes fail open: CUDA-availability assert dropped in CI refactor
verdicts.reasoning: Verified the whole chain against the tree and git history. 847b464e ('ci: make Triton kernel validation blocking on GPU', #476, closing #424) added '- name: Assert CUDA available / python3 -c "import torch; assert torch.cuda.is_available(), ..."' to the GPU legs; git show 76e013d8^:.github/workflows/reusable-python-tests.yml:6-10,70-72 shows the step surviving as an 'assert-cuda' input; 76e013d8 ('ci: unify validation matrices across pipelines', #600) deleted reusable-python-tests.yml and its replacement .github/workflows/python-tests.yml has no equivalent step (read in full; steps are checkout, setup-rust, setup-python, setup-uv, install deps, run test group, upload coverage). A case-insensitive grep for 'is_available|Assert CUDA|nvidia-smi' across .github/ (workflows, actions, scripts) returns nothing. Root conftest.py:37-39 auto-skips every cuda-marked test when torch.cuda.is_available() is False, and skips exit 0; .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh treats only exit 5 specially, so an all-skipped run is indistinguishable from an all-passed run. pr.yml:137-166 and ci.yml:100-138 route all three CUDA lanes (locked / minimum / latest) through python-tests.yml with allow-empty-test-selection: true and rely solely on the marker; ci.yml:151,215-217 make those lanes feed the aggregate gate. Severity medium is right: no runtime or privacy impact, but the only GPU validation of Triton kernels, patched-model parity, and CUDA DP paths can report green indefinitely on a broken runner. No open issue covers it (#424 is closed; #325/#330/#429 are different scopes).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: GPU-runner-001 loses CUDA (driver/toolkit mismatch after a host update). torch.cuda.is_available() returns False, root conftest.py:38 skips every cuda-marked test, pytest exits 0, run_python_test_package.sh records success, and the CUDA (locked), CUDA (minimum dependencies), and CUDA (latest dependencies) lanes in both pr.yml and ci.yml report green, so the required aggregate gate passes and main keeps publishing wheels with zero GPU-side validation. Nothing in .github/ distinguishes 'all skipped' from 'all passed' any more -- the preflight assert added by 847b464e for exactly this reason was dropped when 76e013d8 replaced reusable-python-tests.yml with python-tests.yml.

verdicts.title: rng.md still teaches TypeError-raising gaussian_noise calls (OPQ-141 unfixed)
verdicts.reasoning: Verified line by line. docs/reference/rng.md:309 is 'noise_fn, state = gaussian_noise(1.1, key=noise_key)' inside an otherwise concrete 'Training loop with per-step DP randomness' block; gaussian_noise is declared keyword-only (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:156-164, bare '*' before noise_multiplier), and executing the call raises 'TypeError: gaussian_noise() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 positional argument (and 1 keyword-only argument) were given' (run this session). Lines 380, 401, 412, 415 and 419 bind the documented (noise_fn, state) 2-tuple to a single name, while :332 in the same file uses the correct 'noise_fn, _ = ...' form. Closed issue #416 ('Execute documentation examples and validate public factory signatures') left no executable-docs check: .github/scripts/ has no snippet runner, pr.yml's docs job is only 'mkdocs build --strict' (pr.yml:273-287), and pyproject.toml's pytest config has no doctest-glob, so nothing would catch this. Mitigating: the five tuple-binding lines all pass a literal Ellipsis ('gaussian_noise(..., key=...)'), which is visibly elided pseudo-code and would fail on the '...' first; only :309 is a copy-pasteable snippet that fails on the signature itself. Low severity, docs-only, no epsilon impact. No open issue tracks it (#324 'Make documentation and published claims mechanically verifiable' is a broader programme, not this drift).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user copies the 'Training loop with per-step DP randomness' block from docs/reference/rng.md:302-313 and gets TypeError('gaussian_noise() takes 0 positional arguments...') because the factory is keyword-only -- confirmed by executing the call. The five later snippets (:380, :401, :412, :415, :419) additionally bind the (noise_fn, state) 2-tuple to a single name, teaching a shape that yields "'tuple' object is not callable" if transplanted into real code; these are elided pseudo-code ('...' as the first argument), so they mislead rather than run. Loud, immediate failures in every case; docs-only, no computed privacy value is affected.
